Now I'll make the pending custom model ID commit on save.

The problem is that when a user types a custom model ID but doesn't press "+" or Enter before submitting the form, that pending input gets lost. I need to handle this by merging the pending custom model text into the enabled models during form submission. Since the `customModelInput` state lives at the component level, I can access it in the form's onSubmit handler, and because TanStack's useForm options are defined inline, the closure should capture the latest value from the current render.

A cleaner approach is to intercept the form's native onSubmit event, commit the pending custom model first by setting the form field value directly, then call the form's handleSubmit — this avoids any closure issues since the form's setFieldValue is synchronous and will be read immediately when handleSubmit runs. I'll extract a top-level function that uses the form's getFieldValue and setFieldValue methods so I can reuse it in both the field handler and the form submission. Updating the form state synchronously, so the field will reflect the changes immediately. Now I'll apply these edits to the form submission and field rendering.
Now I'll drop the duplicated local handler in favor of the shared one.
